weather_report:
South Perth drifts into early afternoon under a soft grey lid, the sun a shy rumor behind high, stubborn cloud. The day feels muted and even, edges rounded off, the river wearing a pewter sheen; clarity is gentle rather than sharp. Forecasts keep the ceiling in place through the afternoon and toward evening, so sunshine will be fleeting at best. UV is softened by the overcast but not banished; midday can still nip at bare skin if you linger.

It’s a day for light layers and easy fabrics, a breathable long-sleeve or a light jacket in case the breeze freshens; sunglasses are optional, sunscreen sensible. With the glare tamed, walking errands feel pleasant—an unhurried loop along the foreshore, a quiet ferry crossing to the city and back, or a deliberate browse of the corner grocer. Indoors, it’s a fine time to sort a drawer, polish a pair of shoes, or brew something steady on the stove while the sky keeps its cool, silvery mood.
